1.explanation:
1. src/js/components/DataChart/README.md – the official DataChart documentation, which describes the chart prop, series, and guides, including baseline/zero-line behavior.  
2. src/js/components/DataChart/DataChart.js – the implementation of the DataChart component itself, where negative-value handling and baseline calculation should occur.  
3. src/js/components/DataChart/stories/typescript/Simple.tsx – a baseline story demonstrating positive-value behavior, useful to compare against the broken negative-value case.  
4. src/js/components/DataChart/stories/typescript/Bars.tsx – the example story showing bar charts in DataChart, which is directly relevant when reproducing the bug with negative bars.  
5. src/js/components/Chart/README.md – the underlying Chart component docs, since DataChart delegates actual drawing to Chart and negative-value rendering may need Chart configuration.  
6. src/js/components/Chart/stories/bar.js – Chart’s own bar chart story, to see how the base Chart renders negative bars and whether special axes or guides are required there.
1.bug_scenario: The user is creating a DataChart with bar (and line/point) series and some of the data points are negative. When all data values are positive (e.g. [0, 2, 54]), the DataChart displays the axes, the zero‐line guide, and the bars/points/lines correctly (first screenshot). However, if any data value is negative (e.g. amount: -2), the entire chart area comes up blank (second screenshot). The expected behavior is that the DataChart should still render, drawing a zero baseline and showing negative‐value bars (or lines) below the axis, possibly with a distinct color for negative values.
